item.title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on. In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working. Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. “For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie) Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.” Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.” May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable. “You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote. “One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.” She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.” She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!” Vanguard News The post ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them. The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident. Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains. Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices. “For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said. When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise. “No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said. Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities. “People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said. He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom. According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support. “My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added. item.title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football. In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job. “It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.” The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last. “Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.” Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League. In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid. “If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’” Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns. “Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles. item.title: Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani
item.description: Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country. Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose political choices or opinions differ from theirs, rather than condemn such acts irrespective of the victims’ affiliations. He stated this on X on Wednesday following the campaign violence that reportedly left four persons dead in Delta State. Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps. “The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote. He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side. “Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said. The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved. He cited reports of attacks involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi and President Bola Tinubu in Abuja, saying some media outlets used different descriptions for incidents involving the two political figures. “Some media Houses have even crafted a beautiful way of reporting political violence…POLITICAL THUGS attacked Atiku in Kebbi while ANGRY YOUTHS attacked Tinubu at Abuja Mosque,” he added. Sani’s comments come amid growing concerns over political violence and intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, with incidents involving political supporters raising questions about the safety of campaign activities and the role of political parties in preventing attacks. item.title: 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war in 1970. He noted that at the end of the civil war, the federal government had announced the policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation to rebuild Igbo land, alleging that successive administrations failed to implement the policy. The Deputy Speaker stated that Tinubu is the only president that has made meaningful efforts in implementing the policy by establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC) and putting up infrastructural projects and political appointments across the South East zone. Kalu, who stated this in Umuahia during the donation of 25 vehicles to the Abia State chapter of the Door to Door mobilisation by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, urged the Igbo to re-elect the president to finish his job in the next four years. “For over 50 years, nobody was able to fulfil the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war. Gone are the days of promise. Today, President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise he has given the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He has also given the SEDC the permission to open what is known as the South East Investment Company. And he has funded the company with billions of Naira. “Today, the company has started the project of piping gas across the Southeast. The companies in Lagos and Kano will start coming to build in the Southeast. This is the president that Tompolo wants us to support. “Across the South East, more roads are springing up because our son is the Minister of Works, Engr Dave Umahi. I can’t remember the last time an Igbo man was the Minister of Works. Umahi has been making us proud. The President also appointed Ojukwu as the Minister of Foreign Affairs and another Igbo as the Chief of Naval Staff. The Minister of State for Finance is also an Igbo. “The President has also invested money in securing our lives and properties. The Ministry of Defence budget has increased; employment in the military and police is increasing. The president has also supported state police. Salaries are not being owed because Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy and released more money for the sub-nations. He urged the Igbo to reject anyone who is campaigning for the South East zone to serve for only a four-year term, stressing that when the time comes, the zone would take eight years, as others have done. “Reject them when they come to you that they have signed an agreement for the Igbo to serve for only four years. The Igbo will not wait after 60 years to receive power for only four years. We didn’t wait for 60 years for the Igbo to take only half the bread. Other zones have done right years; when the time comes, the Igbo will take eight years, not four years.” The post 2027: Tinubu has fulfilled promise made to Igbo after civil war – Kalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Osubi Airport simulates air crash after 20 years
item.description: …Drill identifies emergency response gaps, need for modern equipment By Egufe Yafugborhi WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its emergency response capabilities and identify areas requiring improvement. The exercise, conducted at about 1:30pm on the airport’s airside, simulated an aircraft crash involving passengers who sustained varying degrees of injuries. Several emergency response agencies participated in the drill, including the Nigerian Navy Hospital and Air Station Fire Service, Nigeria Police Force, Delta State Fire Service, Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Delta Procare Hospital, Nigerian Ports Authority Health Service and Renaissance Africa Energy Fire Service. Speaking after the exercise, the Airport Manager, Winston Egwuatu, expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying identified operational gaps would be addressed to strengthen the airport’s emergency response capacity. He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures. “No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures. “The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said. Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining. He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment. “Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade. “However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said. The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities. He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident. “It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. item.title: ‘Incoming President’, Titi celebrates Atiku, says ex-VP not tired at 80
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.” In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80”, Chief Amina Titi Atiku Abubakar, the former Second Lady of Nigeria, said she was celebrating “the Incoming President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria come May 29th, 2027 by the Special Grace of God.” “At 80, you are not tired. At 80, your vision for Nigeria is even clearer. I have walked with you through valleys and mountains, and I know what God has placed in you for Nigeria,” she wrote. She said Nigeria needed his “experience,” his “capacity, and your compassionate heart now more than ever.” According to her, this is “reflecting in the enthusiastic and passionate ways Nigerians turned out to cheer you to victory as you articulate your policies and canvass support for your presidential aspiration come January 16, 2027.” Titi said the milestone coincided with 57 years of marriage. “Eighty years of a life well-lived and Fifty-seven years of a love that has stood the test of time. When I first met you as a young lady, I saw a cute, handsome, principled, brilliant, focused Customs officer with big dreams. I did not know I was meeting a destiny.” She credited her husband with the support that led her into the campaign against human trafficking. “Many men would have stopped their wife from confronting human trafficking. You did not. You not only gave me the wings to fly, but the inspiration, the courage, the confidence and the wherewithal to fight for humanity and the vulnerables. You told me, ‘Titi, go and save those girls.'” She said the Women Trafficking and Child Labour Eradication Foundation (WOTCLEF) was born from that encouragement in 1999. “A law was made to criminalize human trafficking in Nigeria and NAPTIP was established to save millions. “The woman I am today – the Lecturer, the Advocate, the Amazing Amazon, the Former Second Lady of Nigeria, the Grand Matron to several Organizations – I am because you allowed me to become,” she said. Titi also paid tribute to Atiku’s record in public service. “Nigeria has known you as a diligent Customs Officer, a successful businessman, a two-term Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria who chaired the National Economic Council that paid off the country’s foreign debt and a democrat who has kept faith with democracy even when it was costly. You don’t just make promises; you build systems. You don’t just talk about privatization and jobs; you did it. “Only few people know how many school fees you pay silently; how many widows you feed daily; how many young people you gave jobs in and out of government, how many lives you have touched directly or indirectly and how many destinies you have transformed positively. item.title: Atiku embraces ‘Daddy Subsidy’ nickname, promises Nigerians relief at 80
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has embraced the nickname “Daddy Subsidy” as he marked his 80th birthday on Wednesday, promising Nigerians that relief would come and pledging to make the country affordable again. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made the remark in a post on X while thanking Nigerians for their birthday wishes and prayers. He said the nickname was among the names Nigerians had given him that he particularly enjoyed, adding that he remained committed to making life easier for citizens. Of all the names Nigerians have given me, "Daddy Subsidy" may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon. To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the… https://t.co/LZo7x3Mgf9 — Atiku Abubakar (@atiku) November 25, 2026 “Of all the names Nigerians have given me, ‘Daddy Subsidy’ may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon,” he wrote. Addressing Nigerians across the country, the former vice-president promised that relief was coming, making an apparent reference to his position on petrol subsidy and the hardship associated with its removal. “To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the barrel. I will make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku added. Atiku’s birthday message comes amid continued political debate over the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which has contributed to increased living and transportation costs. Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Atiku on his 80th birthday, commending his contributions to Nigeria’s political development, democracy, education and the private sector. In a statement issued by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said he shared with Atiku a commitment to democratic pluralism, political participation and allowing Nigerians to present alternative ideas on governance. The president recalled supporting Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition under the defunct Action Congress platform, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to compete and contribute to national discourse. Tinubu also praised Atiku’s investments in education and entrepreneurship, particularly the establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had contributed to expanding access to higher education and developing human capital. Despite their differences in political affiliation and views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability remained important. He wished the former vice-president good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to Nigeria and humanity as he joined the octogenarian club. item.title: Reps order contractor back to failed East-west road culverts
item.description: …Demand urgent repairs, four-week monitoring of project By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along the East-West Road, particularly at Iheke in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Oboku Abonsizibe Oforji, who drew the attention of lawmakers to the reported deterioration of the culverts and the need for urgent intervention to prevent further damage and potential safety risks. The House recalled that it had, on October 3, 2023, adopted a motion on the deplorable condition of the East-West Road, particularly the Iheke axis, following which the Federal Government undertook further interventions. The interventions included the construction of box culverts, approval and release of funds for rehabilitation and flood mitigation works, payments to Rock Result Nigeria Limited and the re-award of the contract to Setraco Nigeria Limited for the continuation of the road dualisation project. However, lawmakers expressed concern over reports that the constructed box culverts had deteriorated, despite the financial commitments made by the government. They said the reported condition of the drainage infrastructure underscored the need for a technical assessment of the works, including the materials used, construction standards and supervision of the project. The House noted that the East-West Road was a major economic and social corridor connecting Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta states to other parts of the country, serving communities and facilitating the movement of people, goods and services. It warned that the deteriorating condition of the road could further disrupt transportation and expose motorists and other road users to safety risks. Lawmakers also expressed concern that the dualisation of the East-West Road from Ahoada in Rivers State through the Bayelsa axis to Patani in Delta State remained incomplete, despite earlier completion targets of April 2025 and November 2025. Consequently, the House urged the Ministry of Works to ensure that Rock Result Nigeria Limited returned to the site without delay to carry out the required rehabilitation or reconstruction of the damaged culverts in accordance with approved engineering standards. It also called for adequate technical supervision, quality assurance and an independent engineering assessment of the remedial works to reduce the risk of further structural problems. In addition, the lawmakers urged the ministry to ensure the completion of the dualisation of the Ahoada-Bayelsa and Patani sections of the road by Setraco Nigeria Limited. The House mandated its Committee on Works and Legislative Compliance to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. item.title: YABATECH non-teaching staff threaten indefinite strike
item.description: …Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday By Adesina Wahab Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met. The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi. They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages. Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff. He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly. “I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said. Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment. He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions. According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment. He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled. “In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. Here at YABATECH, teaching staff have been paid leaving us in the lurch like orphans. We are not less human than teaching staff. We have contacted our management here and last Wednesday, they promised to pay. A week has passed and nothing has happened,” he said. The union chairman questioned why the management had been able to pay teaching staff but had yet to settle the entitlements of non-teaching employees. He said the rising cost of living had worsened the hardship faced by workers, citing the daily transport expenses incurred by some staff members who commute from areas such as Ikorodu to the college. item.title: Reps seek clarification over mining marshals’ letter to lawmaker
item.description: …Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga. The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites. The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas. The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals. In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining. Reading an excerpt from the letter, Gaza said the language used in the correspondence raised concerns about the manner in which a serving member of the National Assembly was addressed. The letter stated: “While we respect the rules of lawmaking in shaping the society through oversight legislative functions, we strongly view the action of Abdulmalik Danga as anti-government and motivated by illegal mining cartels whose unlawful activities are being disrupted by the sanity being restored in the mining sector.” The committee members questioned the basis for the assertions and whether the correspondence reflected an authorised institutional position of the NSCDC. Responding, Onoja told the committee that he wrote the letter in his personal capacity as Commander of the Mining Marshals and did not intend to challenge the constitutional powers of the legislature. He said: “Mr. Chairman, permit me to state clearly on record. My response, my letter, in my personal capacity as the Commander Mining Marshals, is not in any way looking into the legislative powers of the Committee. The letter is speaking to the motion as moved.” Gaza, however, questioned the explanation, particularly because the correspondence was written on NSCDC letterhead and carried an official reference number. The committee chairman consequently asked the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Abubakar Audi, to clarify whether the letter represented the official position of the Corps or was issued without institutional authorisation. Audi said the Corps had administrative procedures requiring officers to obtain approval before issuing correspondence on behalf of the Commandant-General. item.title: ₦1.45trn Lagos ports upgrade targets 20,000 jobs
item.description: …As FG flags off Apapa, Tin Can modernisation By Efe Onodjae The Federal Government on Wednesday flagged off a £746 million (about ₦1.45 trillion) modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos, targeting 48-hour cargo clearance and the creation of 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The project is expected to reduce cargo delays, lower logistics costs and improve Nigeria’s competitiveness in global trade. Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, who performed the groundbreaking at Tin Can Island Port, said the upgrade had become urgent as cargo throughput had outgrown existing port infrastructure. Oyetola said Nigeria’s cargo throughput had increased from 8.11 million metric tonnes in 1977 to 129.3 million metric tonnes, while merchandise trade had risen from $17 billion to over $100 billion annually. He said the project would involve rehabilitation of quay walls and berths, dredging of navigation channels, improved access facilities and installation of modern cargo-handling equipment. According to him, cargo dwell time at Nigerian ports had historically ranged between 10 and 18 days, compared with three to five days at leading international ports, costing the economy an estimated $4 billion annually. He said the upgrade would attract international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo and expand transshipment opportunities. Also speaking, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, described the project as Nigeria’s largest sovereign export credit transaction since 2009. He said the financing arrangement demonstrated international investor confidence in Nigeria’s economic reforms. Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, assured that the project would be delivered in line with approved designs, engineering standards and contractual timelines. item.title: Tinubu pledges to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri MAIDUGURI — President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 70 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Technical School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State. Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesday in Maiduguri while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East Zonal Rally held at the El-Kanemi Sports Centre. The President said his administration remained committed to rescuing the children abducted by suspected Boko Haram terrorists and defeating insurgency in the North-East. “We shall do everything possible to rescue the schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa communities,” he said. The abductions, which occurred in the first quarter of 2026, involved more than 30 children, including toddlers, from Mussa and over 40 students from Lassa. Tinubu also acknowledged the sacrifices of military personnel and other security operatives, particularly those serving on the frontline, assuring them of government support in the fight against terrorism. “The present administration under my leadership acknowledges the sacrifices of troops, especially those at the frontline. Therefore, government would do its best to support our security operatives to defeat terrorism in this region,” he said. On his second-term ambition, the President thanked the people of the North-East for their support for the APC-led administration, promising to consolidate on its achievements if re-elected in 2027. He described Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who hails from Borno State, as a dependable ally and commended Governor Babagana Zulum for his administration’s development efforts. Tinubu particularly cited the newly constructed International Conference Centre in Maiduguri and other projects he commissioned during his visit. Earlier, Zulum thanked the President for choosing Maiduguri as the venue for the zonal rally, expressing satisfaction with the large turnout and orderly conduct of APC supporters. He said Borno State had benefited significantly from the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The governor disclosed that the Federal Government had commenced construction of the Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri road, while also highlighting the establishment of the Federal Polytechnic, Monguno; Federal College of Education, Gwoza; and Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship, Bama. Zulum urged residents of Borno and other states in the North-East to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. The rally attracted seven governors from the region, including Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State. Also in attendance were the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima; former governors; ministers; members of the National Assembly and other APC stakeholders. item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack invest
